sights.w: National Historic Landmark department-store palace whose Grand Court houses the Wanamaker Organ, the world's largest operating musical instrument (28,750 pipes); after Macy's closed in 2025 the new owners brought back performances and the Christmas Light Show (Inquirer, Philly Mag 2025).
The oldest operating theatre in the US (1808) and a National Historic Landmark — first gas footlights in 1837; still stages plays and Tony-winning musicals each season.
Rare-book house museum near Rittenhouse holding Joyce's handwritten Ulysses manuscript, Lewis Carroll's own Alice and a first-edition Don Quixote (Visit Philly; Philly Mag Best of Philly).
One of William Penn's five original squares, revived 20 years ago with a carousel, Philly-landmark mini golf and the winter Chinese Lantern Festival (Visit Philly; Inquirer 2026).
James Logan's c.1730 Georgian estate — both Washington and Howe headquartered here around the Battle of Germantown; on the Historic Germantown OnePass (Visit Philly; Billy Penn 2026).
Philadelphia's only Victorian house museum (1859), open Fri-Sun (Visit Philly Germantown guide; Hidden City).
Free 55-acre Quaker-abolitionist Cope family estate opened to the public in 1916 — 2,000+ trees, a working farm and gardens (Visit Philly; Hidden City).
1775 schoolhouse, Philadelphia's first English-language school and an 1839 abolitionist meeting place; tours second Saturdays May-Oct (Visit Philly Black-history guide).

sights.address: Thomas Mill Rd at Forbidden Drive, Wissahickon Valley Park, Philadelphia, PA 19118
sights.w: The Wissahickon's red covered bridge on the Orange Trail, loved enough to get its own Inquirer column of love letters (Atlas Obscura; Inquirer; Philly Mag Wissahickon guide).

Revolutionary War fort at the mouth of the Schuylkill whose 1777 siege bought Washington time — barracks, blacksmith shop and weekend cannon demonstrations, open Wed-Sun March to mid-December (Visit Philly; Atlas Obscura unusual history).
Swedish-American culture museum tucked into FDR Park, near the site of the 1640s New Sweden colony (Visit Philly hidden gems).

National Historic Landmark and one of the finest Greek Revival buildings in America; its museum tells the story of Stephen Girard and the school's desegregation fight (open Wed-Fri; Visit Philly Black-history guide).

sights.address: Frankford Ave over Pennypack Creek, Holmesburg, Philadelphia, PA 19136
sights.w: Built in 1697 — the oldest surviving roadway bridge in the US and probably the country's oldest stone arch bridge, still carrying Frankford Ave traffic (Atlas Obscura; Inquirer).
75+ of the world's rarest racing sports cars collected by Dr. Fred Simeone over 50 years — a one-of-a-kind museum by the airport (Visit Philly hidden gems).

sights.n: John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge at Tinicum
sights.w: Pennsylvania's largest freshwater tidal marsh, 10+ miles of trails and Darby Creek paddling inside the city limits (Visit Philly hidden gems).

The 1934 Neoclassical rail palace — limestone façade, prism-glass windows and the bronze Angel of the Resurrection WWII memorial; on Architectural Digest's most-beautiful-stations list (Visit Philly architecture guide).

sights.n: Fisher Fine Arts Library & Arthur Ross Gallery
sights.w: Frank Furness's red sandstone and terra-cotta Venetian Gothic library on Penn's campus, home to the Arthur Ross Gallery (Visit Philly University City guide).

Once Pennsylvania's largest burial ground (85,000 graves, 200 acres, Betsy Ross's former resting place), now being reclaimed from the woods by the volunteer Friends of Mount Moriah (Visit Philly strange & unusual guide).
Horace Trumbauer's Art Deco theatre in Glenside, still booking major music, theatre and comedy acts (Visit Philly Jenkintown guide).
1722 manor of Pennsylvania governor William Keith, later seized from loyalist Henry Fergussen and poet Elizabeth Graeme; house and gardens open year-round (Valley Forge Tourism).

sights.address: 553 S Bethlehem Pike, Fort Washington, PA 19034
sights.w: Early-Georgian mansion (1743-48) built by Quaker Samuel Morris — HQ of Washington's Surgeon General during the Whitemarsh Encampment (Valley Forge Tourism).
1704 home of Charles Thomson, Secretary of the Continental Congress and designer of the Great Seal, set in a park with gardens (Valley Forge Tourism).
Reconstruction of the boarding house at 7th & Market where Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence in 1776 — part of Independence National Historical Park (NPS).
Dolley Madison's home with her first husband John Todd Jr. before his 1793 death — a restored middle-class Quaker house in Independence NHP (NPS).
The 1787 townhouse of Bishop William White, first Episcopal bishop of Pennsylvania — an upper-class counterpart to the Todd House in Independence NHP (NPS).
The smallest unit of the National Park System — the Society Hill boarding house where Polish patriot and Revolutionary War engineer Thaddeus Kościuszko lived in 1797-98 (NPS).
Federal-style 1790-91 building in the Independence Hall complex that housed the US Supreme Court from 1791 to 1800 (NPS Independence NHP).
NPS-preserved 18th-19th-century iron-making village in the hills by French Creek State Park — furnace, ironmaster's house and orchards (National Park Service).

sights.address: 32 W Bridge St, New Hope, PA 18938
sights.w: Heritage line between New Hope and Lahaska with antique coaches pulled by a 1925 Baldwin steam locomotive from the Witch's Hat Station (Visit Bucks County).
134 acres with nearly 1,000 native plant species, meadow, pond and a nationally recognised native-plant nursery; reservations required (Visit Bucks County).

sights.n: Pearl S. Buck House (Green Hills Farm)
sights.w: National Historic Landmark homestead of Nobel laureate Pearl S. Buck, with guided house tours (Visit Bucks County).

sights.address: Hermit Ln trail, Wissahickon Valley Park, Philadelphia, PA 19128
sights.w: Stone-fronted hillside cave of the 1694 'Hermits of the Wissahickon' doomsday mystics led by Johannes Kelpius, on the trails at the park's south end (Atlas Obscura; Visit Philly strange & unusual; Hidden City).
Canal-edged former mill-town main street with ~275 shops, galleries, bars and restaurants, next to the Manayunk Canal towpath and the Schuylkill (Visit Philly; Inquirer Manayunk guide).

sights.address: Lemon Hill Dr & Poplar Dr, East Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, PA 19130
sights.w: Neoclassical Fairmount Park villa with oval rooms and curved doors on all three floors — one of the four park houses open for tours (Hidden City; Philadelphia Museum of Art park-house guides).

sights.address: Ford Rd & Greenland Dr, East Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, PA 19121
sights.w: c.1756 Georgian mansion of merchant William Coleman, Franklin's confidant, with one of the city's finest carved overmantels; open for tours (Visit Philly).

sights.address: Edgeley Dr, East Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, PA 19121
sights.w: c.1767 Georgian 'Randolph House' high above the Schuylkill — the most visible of the park houses and one of four open for tours (Hidden City).

sights.n: National Shrine of St. John Neumann
sights.w: Lower church of St. Peter the Apostle holding the glass tomb of St. John Neumann, fourth bishop of Philadelphia and the first American man canonized — founder of the US diocesan school system (Visit Philly sacred-sites trail).
The nation's largest ceramic-arts organisation (founded ~50 years ago), now in a purpose-built Kensington home with exhibitions and classes (Visit Philly off-the-beaten-path museums; Inquirer).

130-year-old Victorian high-rise at Broad & Fairmount, one of the country's first racially integrated hotels, reopened after a $44M restoration with residences and a restaurant (Visit Philly North Broad guide).

sights.n: Fairmount Park Horticulture Center & Centennial Arboretum
sights.address: 100 N Horticultural Dr, West Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, PA 19131
sights.w: Greenhouse and arboretum on the site of the 1876 Centennial Exposition's Horticultural Hall, beside Shofuso (Visit Philly North Philly guide).

Oscar Hammerstein I's 1908 opera house, restored as a year-round concert and comedy venue (Live Nation since 2018) — neoclassical façade, chandeliers and tiered seating (Visit Philly North Broad guide).
El Centro de Oro's 50-year-old Puerto Rican arts and culture centre — gallery, performance and education space (Visit Philly North Philly / Latino sites guides).

Opened for the 1976 Bicentennial as the first museum built by a major US city to preserve African American heritage; permanent exhibit 'Audacious Freedom: African Americans in Philadelphia 1776-1876' (Visit Philly).

sights.n: Weitzman National Museum of American Jewish History
sights.address: 101 S Independence Mall E, Philadelphia, PA 19106
sights.w: The only US museum dedicated exclusively to the American Jewish experience, on Independence Mall; renovating in 2026 with 'The First Salute' (Jewish connections to the Revolution) on view through April 2027 (Visit Philly).
Old City museum on American diversity and liberty, centred on Dale Chihuly's 21-ft glass 'Flame of Liberty' (Visit Philly).
